items.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022
items.q: So I engaged Gio, I engaged Jai Florada. ... So with Gio’s help and Jai’s help and Cathy’s research we went back into a lot of these films

ctx.x: Hmm. How about saxophone spelled wrong?

Bingo. Okay? I mean we’ve seen it all. But again you know then there’s a couple of real interesting things there. One is there’s a tendency in the production cycle, and I’ve seen this, for the artist, who is so eager to get the album done and get the album out okay, that certain things tend to not get as much scrutiny as let’s say the musical side of it. So I’ll say to an artist or an author, “Look if you were doing an album you wouldn’t want clams on your record” Okay? I mean really bad clams, okay? Not just…

just sent a book down, no names, I sent it down to Jai Florada and he said, “What the hell did you do with this book, there’s rubber bands all around?” I said, “Well when you read it you’ve got to hold like one page at a time because they used such an inferior production facility, but the book is wonderful. It’s great.” So that’s something that you encounter more so in the book side of it you know. I don’t want to make this like a plug but I’ll give you a really good example. Joe LaBarbera, who I know you know…
